question: How does simmering differ from boiling?

Simmering has gentle small bubbles (185°F-200°F) while boiling has vigorous large bubbles (212°F)
Simmering uses oil while boiling uses water
answer: Simmering has gentle small bubbles (185°F-200°F) while boiling has vigorous large bubbles (212°F)
explanation: Simmering maintains lower heat for delicate cooking.
